event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: YUM’s 2023 Form 10-K depicts COVID-19 as both a recently-experienced shock and a continuing threat.  Management acknowledges concrete impacts already suffered—store closures, reduced operating hours, mobility restrictions, supply-chain bottlenecks, and labour shortages—and notes that these effects persisted through 2022 (especially in China).  The wording repeatedly stresses materiality (“has had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect”) and emphasises that some government mandates remain in force.  Although no hard dollar figures are supplied, the company links the pandemic to revenue pressure, cost inflation, and operational disruption across its global franchise network.  Statements are forward-looking as well, citing uncertainty about future outbreaks, vaccine efficacy, and evolving regulations; thus risk is framed as both realised and prospective.  Because the filing date (27 Feb 2023) is less than three years after the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic, the Time-Decay Principle allows elevated severity scores.  Overall, the disclosures indicate a high but not catastrophic risk—specific impacts are enumerated, yet no quantified loss is provided and some mitigation (vaccines, reopening trends) is implicit—warranting mid-to-upper‐range micro-scores for individual sentences.

evidence_list.snippet: The coronavirus (COVID-19) global pandemic has had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on our business, growth prospects and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicitly links COVID-19 to adverse business effects already realised.
States the impact is continuing/forward-looking (‘may continue’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct statement of realised and ongoing adverse impact, but generic and unquantified.

evidence_list.snippet: Developments related to the COVID-19 global pandemic have had, and may continue to have, adverse impacts on our business, growth prospects and results of operations.

components.reason: Reinforces historical and potential future harm tied to COVID-19 ‘developments’.
Covers multiple corporate dimensions (business, growth, results).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Confirms past and future risk across several metrics; still broad—no detail or numbers.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of the pandemic, governmental authorities implemented measures to reduce the spread of COVID-19, some of which remain in place today.

components.reason: Identifies government restrictions as a causative operational risk factor.
Notes persistence of restrictions (‘remain in place today’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights continuing external constraints that can impair operations.

evidence_list.snippet: These measures have included, and in some instances continue to include restrictions on travel outside the home and limitations on business and other activities as well as encouraging social distancing.

components.reason: Details specific restrictions (travel, business limits, social distancing).
Mentions their ongoing nature (‘continue to include’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete examples of restrictions but stops short of linking to financial magnitude.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of the pandemic, we and our Concepts’ franchisees have experienced store closures and reduced store-level operations, including reduced operating hours and dining room closures.

components.reason: Specifies operational disruptions: store closures, reduced hours, dining-room shutdowns.
Indicates both company-owned and franchisee impact (system-wide reach).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete, system-wide operational harm raises severity.

evidence_list.snippet: The impact on our sales in each of our markets has been dependent on the timing, severity and duration of the outbreak, measures implemented by government authorities as well as our reliance on dine-in sales in the market.

components.reason: Connects sales volatility directly to outbreak characteristics and restrictions.
Highlights vulnerability of dine-in dependent markets.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows sales sensitivity to pandemic variables, but lacks quantified effect.

evidence_list.snippet: During 2022, COVID-19 outbreaks and resulting government restrictions limiting mobility continued to impact sales in certain key markets such as China.

components.reason: Provides contemporaneous evidence (2022) of sales impact.
Mentions a major market (China), signalling material exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Recent, market-specific impact underscores ongoing severity.

evidence_list.snippet: We are unable to fully predict the impact that COVID-19 will have on our and our Concepts’ franchisees’ operations going forward due to various uncertainties, including the severity and duration of the pandemic and future outbreaks of COVID-19, the timing, availability, acceptance and effectiveness of medical treatments and vaccines, the spread of potentially more contagious and/or virulent forms of COVID-19, and actions that may be taken by governmental authorities.

components.reason: Emphasises forward-looking uncertainty across multiple variables.
Lists uncontrollable factors (variants, vaccine uptake, government action).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures breadth of future risk drivers, albeit without numbers.

evidence_list.snippet: Furthermore, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, there are now stricter health regulations and guidelines and increased public concern over food safety standards and controls.

components.reason: Identifies new regulatory burden and reputational risk stemming from pandemic.
Highlights ongoing compliance costs and consumer perception issues.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows secondary risks (regulation, reputation) but less direct financial linkage.

evidence_list.snippet: Additional risks include the impact of import restrictions or controls, sanctions, foreign exchange control regimes (including restrictions on currency conversion), health guidelines and safety protocols related to the COVID-19 pandemic, labor costs and conditions, compliance with the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the UK Bribery Act and other similar applicable laws prohibiting bribery of government officials and other corrupt practices, and the laws and policies that govern foreign investment in countries where our Concepts’ restaurants are operated.

components.reason: Places COVID-19 health protocols among a list of global operational risks.
Links pandemic guidelines to cross-border operational complexity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: COVID-19 is one of several cited factors; mention is broad and less impactful.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced and may continue to experience, certain supply chain disruptions resulting from, among other things, capacity, transportation, staffing and operational challenges associated with the pandemic and the current macroeconomic environment, which have adversely affected and may continue to adversely affect our business, growth prospects and results of operations.

components.reason: Directly attributes supply-chain disruptions to the pandemic.
Acknowledges both past and future adverse effects on business performance.
Enumerates specific disruption drivers (capacity, transportation, staffing).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed, multi-facet operational impact tied to pandemic yields high severity.

evidence_list.snippet: Throughout 2022, 2021 and 2020 we had a significant number of restaurants that were temporarily closed including restaurants closed due to government and landlord restrictions as a result of COVID-19.

components.reason: Offers three-year evidence of widespread temporary closures linked to COVID-19.
Covers both governmental and landlord-imposed restrictions, expanding risk scope.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Historic and ongoing closures illustrate material operational disruption.

evidence_list.snippet: Moreover, franchisee noncompliance with our franchise agreements may reduce the overall customer perception and goodwill of our Concepts’ brands, including by failing to meet health and safety standards (e.g., additional sanitation protocols and guidelines connected to the COVID-19 pandemic), to engage in quality control or maintain product consistency, or to comply with cybersecurity requirements, or through the participation in improper business practices.

components.reason: Connects pandemic-driven sanitation protocols to potential brand damage.
Expands risk to franchise compliance and reputation.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Reference is indirect and focused on compliance, so relative severity is lower.
